newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends down with cash, erases gain.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends down with cash, erases gain.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures tumbled toward Wednesday's close, erasing earlier gains and moved in tandem with falling physical power prices in the western U.S.
"There's a general weakness in the cash market. Bids started backing out at the close," said a Houston trader.
Some participants attributed the late sell-off to fading concerns over the operation of a unit at the Palo Verde nuclear generating station near Phoenix, Ariz.,
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde unit 1 was back up to about 80 percent power following repairs to a leak in a small steam pipe.

December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 74 cents at $23.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a session high of $25.30. December COB cash prices were quoted at $23.50-$24.00, down from $25.00-$25.50 earlier today.
January COB 1997 ended down 76 cents at $21.12 after being traded between $20.75 and $22.25. Deferred COB months finished mostly five to 50 cents higher.
The futures and cash electricity market shrugged off news of Bonneville Power Administration's ongoing refrain from selling surplus power.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures finished down 38 cents at $22.10 after reaching as high as $24.25. December cash PV were talked at $22.00-$22.25, off from $24.00-$24.25 earlier.
January 1997 PV ended down 17 cents at $19.50 after bouncing between $19.00 and $21.00. Outer PV contracts finished mostly flat to 25 cents higher.

"As long as gas is volatile this time of the year so will power be," the Houston trader said, adding natgas prices at the San Juan/Blanco Hub finished the day unchanged from Tuesday after rising briefly.
Spot natgas values in other parts of the U.S. generally rose ten cents per million British thermal units on forecasts on cold weather this weekend.
NYMEX estimated 207 COB and 187 PV contracts were sold.
